ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a parallelogram ABCD, with point A at the upper right, point B at the lower right, point C at the lower left, and point D at the upper left. The diagonals AC and BD are drawn in the figure and intersect at point F. At point A, AC divides ∠DAB into two parts, 20° and 32°; at point B, 40.1° is marked between BD and BC. Then reason: From the figure, ∠DAB = 20° + 32° = 52°. Because opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, ∠BCD = ∠DAB = 52°. In triangle BCD, it is known that ∠DBC = 40.1° and ∠BCD = 52°, so ∠BDC = 180° - 40.1° - 52° = 87.9°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: ABCD is a parallelogram with diagonal BD drawn. At vertex A, diagonal AC splits the interior angle DAB into 20° and 32°, so ∠DAB = 52°. At vertex B, the marked angle between BD and BC is ∠DBC = 40.1°. Since opposite angles in a parallelogram are congruent, ∠BCD = ∠DAB = 52°. Now work in triangle BCD and use the triangle angle sum: ∠BDC = 180° − 40.1° − 52° = 87.9°.
